speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Transport whether the Government will consider not allowing commercial shared personal mobility device (PMD) services until the riding culture for PMDs has improved and incidences of unsafe and inconsiderate usage have subsided.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This will facilitate enforcement and deter reckless riding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: However, more time is required to understand their operational and safety processes as these services are relatively new and rather limited in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned about the new regulations, the registration requirement, and I agree that that may deter reckless riding and illegal riding to some extent.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State what are the current plans to improve better riding etiquette, inconsiderate use of PMD because inconsiderate uses may not amount to an offence?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, a lot of such inconsiderate uses on an everyday basis are not really captured as such.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But I think there is a public relations aspect to this, and I think a lot of, especially pedestrians on the ground, are concerned about this.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Moving forward, what are the Government's plans to improve this aspect?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And allow me to indulge in answering the very pertinent question, which I think many Singaporeans as well as users of PMDs are concerned about.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We adopt a multi-pronged approach to deter reckless riding.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: One of the measures that we have adopted is education initiatives.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have embarked on a public education campaign.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In order to promote gracious sharing of public paths, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) actually launched a wave of communications since early 2017 to raise awareness of the active mobility rules and code of conduct, as well as safe riding habits.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And these safety messages have been translated into various languages, including Mandarin, Malay, Tamil, Hindi and Bengali.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And LTA will continue to raise public awareness of these new active mobility rules as well as the penalties involved if such rules are violated.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And this Safe Riding Programme has actually two components.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There is a practical component whereby the programme teaches participants how to manoeuvre the bicycles and PMDs safely as well as to react to certain unforeseen circumstances.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Of course, there is another component of a didactic lecture which I have already mentioned.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In addition to all these educational initiatives, I think the Member is also aware that we have enacted legislative changes, such as the Active Mobility Act, as well as stepping up enforcement actions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA has their Active Mobility Enforcement Officers who are stepping up their enforcement actions as well as patrols at all these hot spots where there is a high volume of pedestrians and cyclists.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have also engaged volunteers on the ground to look into educating users on safe riding habits as well.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: If this proves to be effective, I think we will extend it to more places.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Right now, we just piloted it to a few areas like in Ang Mo Kio, Yishun and Ubi.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Just a follow-up supplementary question to the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Regarding usage of PMDs, increasingly, we are seeing them being used in private premises, such as shopping malls.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Some of these malls and private places are quite porous, and they allow PMDs to move from public to private spaces.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Many of these mall owners are at a loss.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: We have seen situations where there is confrontation when some of these PMD users say, "This is private premises; it is my freedom to use the PMD.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Why are you telling me not to?" So, are there measures taken to work with mall owners and perhaps even give more powers to them to help them in that journey to enforce, minimise or eradicate some of these very dangerous, negligent and careless PMD uses?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Active Mobility Act as well as the Parking Places (Amendment) Act deals with situations within public places.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to the Member's query as to private places, this is really up to the owners of the private places to come up with measures to prevent illegal use of such mobility devices.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Of course, if these private entities need assistance, they can also approach us to step up education to educate PMD users on the right habits as well as riding safety.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the end of the day, because these are private places, it is up to the private landowners to exercise the due diligence in preventing such use of PMDs in those areas.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I have one supplementary question for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Despite all the measures that we have taken to encourage safe riding behaviour, accidents do happen.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And some of these accidents involve my residents.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What would the Senior Minister of State suggest the recourse that the accident victim could take where, let us say, the rider has no insurance coverage and neither does the accident victim?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Some of the medical costs incurred can be quite high and can be very difficult for the accident victim to claim compensation.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In situations where there are accidents, the first thing that the victim has to do is to report it to the Police so that the necessary investigations can be done.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I agree with the Member that, indeed, there has been a rise in the number of accidents involving active mobility devices on public paths.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, I will leave to the Active Mobility Advisory Panel to advise us.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: They will be meeting and we will take reference from them.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: I notice that upon approaching the zebra crossing at every crossroad, it is quite common, at least for me, to see that the PMD riders do not stop but just rush through.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Is there a way that we can do something at the crossing so that they will slow down and not rush through the zebra crossing because their speed is much faster than that of the normal pedestrian's?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: I guess Members know what I mean, right?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As what the Minister has said, indeed, PMD use, as well as reckless driving, have become one of the hotter topics, rather than trains and buses.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Yes, indeed, I think not only at zebra crossings.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Even when the PMD users are actually riding on normal pathways or shared pathways, they have to exercise due diligence and considerations, as well as obey traffic rules.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, public education is important in educating some of these PMD users on how to use the PMDs in a more responsible way.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: If we are able to achieve that, I think it will be much safer for all users, and we will also be able to achieve our vision of a "car-lite" society.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I think the Senior Minister of State has alluded to a lot about encouraging people to use active mobility devices on the back of assumed success of the education programme because we do not have a law now, or we are just having a law in place.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I want to ask how effective has this education programme been.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: First, how many have taken the safe riding programme?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This is so that we know that the educational efforts are making an impact and that we can count on them to make sure that the use of active mobility devices is safe.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Besides public education, I think there are also other measures that LTA and the Ministry of Transport are implementing to make sure that the use of PMDs is safe on our paths.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, I urge Members, as well as all Singaporeans, to be a little bit more patient.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will definitely want to step up the public education efforts.
